correctness.rationale: Basu–Majumdar–Rosso stationarity gives positive integral tau=2v int e^{2gamma G}/(v²-f²) dx. Twice differentiating gives strictly positive second derivative for gamma>0. Endpoint singularity forces divergence at gamma→0, while a region with G>0 forces divergence for gamma→∞, proving a unique global minimizer. Blow-up at the coalescing inner barrier yields gamma tau contribution e^z−1 and the remote support endpoint yields e^z, a crucial second layer. Uniform compact-scale convergence plus exclusion of gamma/delta→0,∞ proves the optimizers converge to the unique stationary point of (2e^z−1)/z. Independent numerical ODE quadrature at three subcritical epsilons gave successive convergence of optimized proxy to leading prediction; numerical checks cannot certify uniform asymptotics.
residual_risks: Only the stationary-density proxy for 1D noiseless symmetric quartic run-and-tumble model below critical barrier; not a general MFPT or interacting-particle theorem.

originality.rationale: Original Basu–Majumdar–Rosso stationary density and fixed-positive-gamma VFT divergence are prior work and explicitly acknowledged. Their inspected primary treatment documents a numerical optimum but not uniqueness for every subcritical a or the simultaneous singular gamma∼sqrt(epsilon) limit with two contributing layers. Guéneau–Majumdar–Schehr analyze exact MFPT, which is a different observable; no conflation. An implicit optimization of their integral in another source remains possible.
